data.title: AS-75 F3/F4: an in-flight deploy reports as a crashed watcher, and its log file is empty

data.to:
From the AS-75 QA review (qa-ruben), findings F3 and F4. Both are about what a human sees while a deploy is running.

F3. DEPLOY_STATE_STALE_MS is 10 minutes; deployTimeoutMin is 15; and deploy-state.json is not rewritten during a build. A build lasting 10-15 minutes therefore makes the sidebar say 'the host may be asleep or the watcher crashed' while the watcher is healthy and mid-build — the indicator accuses itself of the one failure it was built to report. Fix is either a heartbeat write during the build or a stale threshold above the timeout, not below it.

F4. logs/deploy-*.log is 0 bytes after a SUCCESSFUL build, because the compose invocation passes --progress quiet. Both READMEs advertise that file as the build output and name it as the remedy when a deploy is in cooldown. The quiet flag was copied from apps/chat/chat, where it exists to protect --json stdout from build noise — an irrelevant concern for a file sink.

ACCEPTANCE. An in-flight deploy never reports as a crashed watcher, and a successful deploy leaves a log with the build output the READMEs promise. Both demonstrated against a real build, not argued from the code.

provenance.reason: Board directive DM msg 557 (2026-09-07): Chat set before further core-product work

data.body:
Implementation done (Marcus, tick watcher:92536 loop tick 5). Branch feat/AS-87-deploy-heartbeat-and-log fast-forwarded onto master 9bd5f7c (post-AS-84 c41ac6a); head 7c80e50; merge-tree clean.

Commits: 3fc3407 source — inflight closure + heartbeat persist({...inflight, reason:'deploying'}) in evaluateInner's deploying branch (returned decision stays busy), --progress plain, BUILD_REASONS.deploying, README reason row, '8 of 9' -> '9 of 10'. 5c65a15 tests — heartbeat (AC-1/2/3/9 in one test, per the plan's AC-2 row), argv exact pin (AC-6), composeBuild pass-through + stale override (AC-4), label sentence (AC-5), opt-in real build watcher-deploy-real.test.js (AC-7/8). 7c80e50 — real-build Dockerfile carries a per-run nonce (see M7).

Cardinality: master (main checkout) 530 tests / 530 pass / 0 skipped — the 522 figure was pre-AS-89. Branch host: 535 tests / 534 pass / 1 skipped (opt-in) / 0 fail. Delta +5, not the plan's +7 (four ACs share one test). Compose predicted 534 total, 533 pass, 1 skipped — NOT RUN in this tick (time box); reviewer takes the --build receipt.

Mutants (each anchored to a unique site, applied asserted, restored, git diff --exit-code clean): M1 delete heartbeat -> red {AS-87 heartbeat} = predicted. M2 persist without inflight -> red {AS-87 heartbeat} = predicted. M3 return reason 'deploying' -> red {AS-87 heartbeat} only; ZERO from watcher-loop.test.js. FINDING for the plan: the loop tests are pure functions of a boolean (nextPollAction) and pendingDeploy() reads lastDecision, which the deploying branch never sets (it returns before the assignment), so the plan's named AC-3 falsifier cannot go red by construction; the AC-3 assertion inside the heartbeat test is the real kill. Pre-existing shape, unchanged here. M4 -> red {api AS-87 composeBuild} = predicted. M5 delete the sentence -> red {AS-75 label prose pin, AS-87 label} = predicted (2). M6 quiet -> red {AS-87 argv} = predicted. M7 real build (ADVANCE_DOCKER_BIN=/usr/local/bin/docker, AS87_REAL_BUILD=1): unmutated PASS in 86 s (>=5 heartbeats all 'deploying', log has AS87-MARKER and a # step line, outcome ok); with M6 applied -> red on 'deploy-*.log is not empty' after a 91 s build = predicted. First M7 attempt went red on '0 heartbeats' in 5.8 s — BuildKit layer cache served the previous run; fixed in 7c80e50 (nonce), a stale-image hazard inside the test itself. NOT RUN: M7-with-M1 (real build, heartbeat red) and M8 (skip-guard removal; its red is the compose container). Progress note: scratchpad/agent-developer-marcus/AS-87-progress.md. Also noted: loop-label's reason-list pin did not include AS-84's 'error' reason; I added only 'deploying' (12 -> 13), left 'error' for AS-88's docs/tidy pass to decide.

Routed in_progress -> review (cto-owen, tick watcher:92536 loop tick 5, --no-auto-review). Marcus: head 7c80e50 (3 commits, rebased onto master post-AS-84), merge-tree clean; host 535 examined / 534 pass / 1 skipped (opt-in real-build) / 0 fail vs master 530 (the plan's 522 baseline predated AS-89; delta +5 not +7 because four criteria share one heartbeat test, as AC-2 allows). 7 of 8 mutants run: M1/M2/M4/M5/M6 exact; M3 red only on the new heartbeat test — the plan's named watcher-loop falsifier cannot go red because pendingDeploy() reads lastDecision, which the deploying branch never sets (plan correction, reviewer to confirm); M7 red on 'log not empty' after a real 91 s build, after a first false red caused by BuildKit cache — fixed with a per-run Dockerfile nonce in 7c80e50. Not run: M7-with-M1 and M8 (skip-guard removal; red is the compose container). No compose receipt — Priya (per plan) takes the counted --build run next tick, predicted 534 total / 533 pass / 1 skipped. Aside for AS-88's docs pass: the loop-label reason pin never picked up AS-84's 'error' reason; only 'deploying' was added here (12 -> 13).

REVIEW AS-87 (Priya, cycle 1, branch feat/AS-87-deploy-heartbeat-and-log head 7c80e50, 3 commits, all developer-marcus <developer-marcus@agents.american-software.local>; no .lattice/ on the branch; merge-tree vs master clean; worktree clean). Verdict: implementation-level rework needed — one blocking finding in the opt-in real-build test; the two production fixes (heartbeat, --progress plain) are correct and demonstrated against real builds.

FINDINGS (before the sweep; 1 blocking, 5 non-blocking)

F1 BLOCKING (implementation-level) — the real-build test's compose project is named `app`, not the temp dir, so its teardown is a no-op and every opt-in run leaks a running container, an image and a network on the host. test/watcher-deploy-real.test.js:28 computes `project` from the temp dir's basename (asc-as87-<pid>-xxxx) and :39 runs `compose -p <that> down --rmi local -v`; but :29 puts compose.yaml in the `app` SUBdirectory and :49 hands that subdirectory to makeDeployOps as appDir, and compose derives the project name from the directory holding compose.yaml — so the real project is `app`. Observed, not argued: after my M7-with-M1 run, `docker compose ls -a` showed project `app` running(1) with config `/private/tmp/asc-as87-26774-zb1388/app/compose.yaml` (a directory the test had already rmSync'd); `docker ps --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=app` showed `app-as87-1 | Up About a minute | working_dir /private/tmp/asc-as87-26774-zb1388/app`; network `app_default` present; image `app-as87:latest` plus the previous run's build left dangling (same tag, moved). The test's own comment at :25-27 ("compose falls back to this temp dir's basename") states the opposite of what compose does. Consequences: (a) plan §2.1 and the amended §8 isolation requirement are not met — `app` is a generic name that would collide with any other compose project called `app` on a developer host, and the live chat stack is protected only by luck of naming; (b) `sleep 3600` containers, `app_default` and dangling images accumulate per run (the address-pool leak the orchestrator warned about); (c) a false comment in the deliverable. Fix shape (implementer's call): make the derived name equal `project` — write compose.yaml/Dockerfile directly in `dir` (appDir = dir), or name the subdirectory after the temp dir — and add a numbered criterion with its falsifier: AC-11 "after the test's t.after, `docker compose ls -a` does not list the project and no container carries label com.docker.compose.project=<project>", red by restoring the `app` subdirectory (M9). The `-p` in the `down` call becomes correct by construction once the names agree, and AS-88's explicit `-p` in makeDeployOps will make it exact. I tore the leaked `app` project down myself under its own labels after M7-with-M6 finished (attributable: every label points at this test), and record that below. I did not fix this inline: it changes the test's behavior and I would be verifying my own patch.

N1 (non-blocking, record correction) — the compose prediction on the task was wrong: predicted 534 total / 533 pass / 1 skipped; actual 535 total / 529 pass / 6 skipped / 0 fail. Five of the six skips are the pre-existing git-less container skips (AS-86 x2, deploy-shape x1, AS-84 entry point x2 — the same five Ruben counted on AS-84's receipt) and the sixth is the opt-in; node counts skipped tests in `tests`, so compose total = host total, not host − 1. Plan §5's "compose N−1" formula is wrong for the same reason.

N2 (non-blocking, backlog) — M8's named red is a 10-minute hang by construction, not a failure. With the skip guard removed and docker unresolvable (the compose container's situation), the test's `while (!ops.isDeploying())` spin at :77 has no exit when the first evaluate() refuses (no-docker, inputs-dirty, no-git), so the only red is the test's own 10-minute timeout. Suggest a fail-fast: await the first evaluate()'s decision with a short race and assert action === 'deploy' before spinning. Host proxy run recorded below.

N3 (non-blocking, follow-up) — loop-label.test.js:178 "every build reason has prose" examines 13 reasons but BUILD_REASONS has 14: AS-84's `error` (loop-status.js:60) is not in the pin. Marcus flagged it and deferred to AS-88; it should be a one-line pin extension on whichever task touches that file next.

N4 (non-blocking, plan correction confirmed) — AC-3's named falsifier cannot go red. M3 (return reason 'deploying' from the deploying branch) reds only the AS-87 heartbeat test's deepEqual; zero from watcher-loop.test.js, because the branch returns before `lastDecision = decision` (advance-watcher.mjs:1138) so pendingDeploy() never sees the deploying-branch decision, and the loop tests are pure functions of booleans. Marcus's correction stands; the plan's AC-3 row should name the heartbeat test's decision assertion as the kill.

N5 (attribution note) — my M4 red set was one wider than predicted ({api AS-87 composeBuild, stream AS-85 build-field frames}); the extra red is my mutant's blast radius (I mapped every reason outside an allowlist to unreadable-state and the AS-85 test drives `stale-state`, which my allowlist omitted), not a guard finding.

PROBES PAST THE LIST (M6)
P1 Production wiring: deployPoll() (advance-watcher.mjs:2573-2577) calls evaluate() unconditionally every deployPollS; the `if (deployOps.isDeploying()) return` at :2454 is the TICK poll, not the deploy poll — the heartbeat reaches production. (By reading; no unit test pins this wiring — AS-84 F6's wiring test covers deployPoll's catch, not the call frequency. Acceptable.)
P2 Ordering race heartbeat-after-final-persist: performDeploy's finally clears `deploying` and the post-deploy persist (:1128) runs in the same microtask continuation as the `await performDeploy` return, before any timer-fired evaluate() can run; the heartbeat unit test asserts `after.reason !== 'deploying'`. No race.
P3 Error path: a throwing deploy() is caught at :1030, finally clears deploying/inflight, so the heartbeat stops with the build. By reading.
P4 Failure-path log under `--progress plain` is a superset: a scratch Dockerfile with `RUN ... && exit 7` through the REAL runDockerCompose: result {code:1}, log 1285 bytes containing the RUN marker, a `#N` BuildKit step line and "did not complete successfully: exit code: 7". (Own scratch project, torn down.)
P5 Is the opt-in test a demonstration or a proxy? Demonstration: it drives the real runDockerCompose and the real makeDeployOps against a real BuildKit build; the fakes (git ls-tree, /api/build fetch) sit outside both findings' mechanisms; cadence 5 s vs production 60 s is the same call shape. What it does not show is the server reading the heartbeat during a live chat-image build — AC-4 covers that at unit level, and the task's acceptance wording is satisfied.

CARDINALITY, then counts
Host master (main checkout, re-derived): 530 examined / 530 pass / 0 skipped / 0 fail. Host branch (worktree): 535 / 534 / 1 skipped (opt-in) / 0 fail; delta +5 as claimed.
Compose receipt: /usr/local/bin/docker compose -p asc-review-as87 run --rm --build test (DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD=1) — "Image asc-review-as87-test Built"; 535 examined / 529 pass / 6 skipped / 0 fail; exit 0; project torn down ("Network asc-review-as87_default Removed").
Real build, unmutated (AS87_REAL_BUILD=1 ADVANCE_DOCKER_BIN=/usr/local/bin/docker, from the worktree): 1 examined / 1 pass in 90.9 s.

MUTANTS — 8 named, 9 runs (M7 is a double), 9 red, 0 survivors. Battery on a scratch copy of apps/chat (never the worktree), each anchored to a unique site (anchor count asserted 1), applied asserted by byte comparison, full host suite per mutant, restored and re-read equal to the original. The scratch copy has one baseline failure of its own (deploy-shape git ls-files, no .git in the copy) which is subtracted from every set below.
M1 delete heartbeat persist -> red {AS-87 heartbeat} = predicted.
M2 persist without ...inflight -> red {AS-87 heartbeat} = predicted.
M3 return reason 'deploying' -> red {AS-87 heartbeat}; watcher-loop 0 (N4).
M4 composeBuild maps unknown reasons -> red {api AS-87 composeBuild, stream AS-85 build-field frames} (N5).
M5 delete BUILD_REASONS.deploying -> red {AS-75 label prose pin, AS-87 label} = predicted (2).
M6 plain -> quiet -> red {AS-87 argv} = predicted.
M7-with-M1 (real build, second scratch copy): red after a 90.9 s build on the heartbeat assertion — actual 'stale-build', expected 'deploying' (the frozen pre-build write). This is the run Marcus reported NOT RUN.
M7-with-M6 (real build, second scratch copy re-copied fresh, M6 applied at the spawn argv, anchor count 1): red after a 90.9 s build on 'deploy-*.log is not empty' (watcher-deploy-real.test.js:104) — the same red Marcus reported, re-derived. F1 observed on this run too: after its t.after ran, `docker compose ls -a` still listed project `app` running(1) with config /private/tmp/asc-as87-30541-FxQGKC/app/compose.yaml and container app-as87-1 "Up 22 seconds"; I then ran `docker compose -p app down --rmi local -v --remove-orphans` plus `docker rmi` on the images labelled com.docker.compose.project=app — container, image app-as87:latest and network app_default removed; nothing labelled `app` remains on the host.
M8 skip guard removed (host proxy for the container red; the container form is a 10-minute hang, N2): control with the guard present and no opt-in -> 1 examined / 1 skipped "opt-in: set AS87_REAL_BUILD=1"; guard removed, same env (ADVANCE_DOCKER_BIN=/nonexistent/docker) -> no result within 25 s, killed ETIMEDOUT — the test runs instead of skipping. Red observed as the hang the guard prevents.
Worktree after everything: git -C .worktrees/AS-87 status --porcelain empty on feat/AS-87-deploy-heartbeat-and-log; scratch copies are mine and outside the tree.

ACCEPTANCE SWEEP — floor check, 10 of 10 pass, with 1 finding outside the list blocking (F1) and 5 notes.
AC-1 pass (heartbeat test; M1 red). AC-2 pass (same test, inflight fields; M2 red). AC-3 pass (returned decision busy; M3 red on the heartbeat test's deepEqual — N4). AC-4 pass (api test; M4 red). AC-5 pass (sentence names deploy-*.log; M5 red). AC-6 pass (exact argv pin; M6 red). AC-7 pass (real build unmutated green; M7-with-M1 red; M7-with-M6 addendum). AC-8 pass (compose run shows 1 skipped opt-in, not a fail; M8 proxy red). AC-9 pass (the :1089 key-set pin untouched in the diff; the heartbeat test asserts key equality). AC-10 pass (host green; compose Built line quoted; cardinality first). README sentences at watch/README.md:42 and :529 and apps/chat/README.md:432 are now true without edits (P4 and the unmutated run's log); the new `deploying` row is in the reason table.

ROUTING: review -> in_progress, rework cycle 1 of 3, implementation-level. Rework scope: F1 (project-name/teardown, plus AC-11 with its M9 red) only; N2 optional in the same pass if cheap; N3/N4 are plan/record edits for the orchestrator or AS-88. Predicted after rework: host 535 or 536 (if N2 adds an assertion it is inside the same test: 535) / compose 535 total / 6 skipped; the opt-in run must additionally leave `docker compose ls -a` without its project.

Routed review -> in_progress, rework cycle 1 of 3 (cto-owen, tick watcher:15881 loop tick 6). Priya: implementation-level rework — production fixes correct and demonstrated on real builds; F1 blocking: watcher-deploy-real.test.js leaks a compose project named 'app' (compose.yaml in a dir/app subdir, teardown names the temp-dir basename). Findings + fix shape + new AC-11/M9 appended to the plan. N2 (fail-fast before the isDeploying spin) may be taken in the same rework; filed as AS-117 regardless. N3 (loop-label pin 13 of 14) filed as AS-118. Marcus resumes in .worktrees/AS-87.

Rework cycle 1 done (Marcus, tick watcher:15881 loop tick 7). Head ddc8833 on feat/AS-87-deploy-heartbeat-and-log (one rework commit on top of 7c80e50); merge-tree against master f90e7a8 clean; 0 .lattice paths on the branch; master had no non-board changes since the branch point.

WHAT CHANGED (apps/chat/test/watcher-deploy-real.test.js only):
- F1: the app directory is now join(dir, project) instead of join(dir, 'app'). compose derives the project from the basename of its cwd, which is appDir (performDeploy passes cwd: appDir to runDockerCompose), not the temp dir above it; naming the subdir after project makes the -p project teardown address what the build created. State file, lock and logs stay outside the build context. Comment at the top of the test rewritten to say that. No COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME pass-through (plan §8 amendment respected).
- AC-11 (new assertions inside the opt-in test): positive control before teardown — 1 container from this run, 1 compose project from this run, >= 1 as87 image examined — then teardown(), then containers [] / compose ls -a [] / no <project>-* image. The probe is keyed on the run's temp-dir basename (container working_dir label, compose ls ConfigFiles), NOT on project, because a leak is exactly a project named differently from what we tear down. teardown() is run-once; t.after still calls it on the failure path.
- N2 TAKEN (AS-117 can be closed as folded in): the while (!isDeploying()) spin now races the first evaluate() settling; a decision that settles before deploying is seen fails with the decision and the watcher log. Demonstrated on a scratch copy whose git fake reports a dirty status: red in 0.73 s with {action:'noop', reason:'inputs-dirty'} — the shape that was a 10-minute hang under Priya's M8.

M9 (restore join(dir, 'app'); scratch copy scratchpad/agent-developer-marcus/mut87/m9-app-subdir.test.mjs importing the worktree's watcher by absolute path; mutation asserted at line 34, original pattern absent): red after 82.4 s, exact failing set = 1: 'AC-11: no container from this run survives teardown', actual ['app-as87-1  project=app  working_dir=/private/tmp/asc-as87-35496-pDa20n/app']. The positive control passed under M9 (the probe saw the mis-named project while up), so the red is the leak itself, not a vacuous probe. The mutant's leaked app project was torn down by hand afterwards (compose -p app down --rmi local -v, exit 0: container, image app-as87:latest, network app_default removed) — attributable by the pid in its working_dir. Worktree git diff --exit-code clean throughout (never mutated).

REAL BUILD (unmutated, AS87_REAL_BUILD=1 ADVANCE_DOCKER_BIN=/usr/local/bin/docker): 1 test examined, 1 pass, 92.8 s. Host leak-check after it and after the compose run: compose ls -a lists only asc-chat, asc-invoicing, bettereads, whatever-sticks (the four present before I started); 0 containers and 0 images with service label as87; 0 asc-review-as87 containers.

COUNTS: host node --test in the worktree — 535 tests, 534 pass, 1 skipped (opt-in), 0 fail. Compose docker compose -p asc-review-as87 run --build --rm test — receipt 'Image asc-review-as87-test Built', 535 tests, 529 pass, 6 skipped (5 git-not-runnable + 1 opt-in), 0 fail, exit 0. Both are ONE BELOW Priya's cycle-2 expectation (536/535/1 and 536/530/6) because AC-11 is written as assertions inside the opt-in real-build test, as the rework instructions asked, not as a separate test — it needs the build to have happened and cannot stand alone, and as a separate opt-in test it would register as a second skip, not a pass. Cycle-1 mutants M1–M8 were not re-run: the rework touches only the opt-in test file and no production code (commit ddc8833 diff is confined to watcher-deploy-real.test.js).

Unrun: M7-with-M1 and M8 (Priya ran both in cycle 1; production code unchanged since).

REVIEW AS-87 (Priya, cycle 2, branch feat/AS-87-deploy-heartbeat-and-log @ ddc8833, tick watcher:15881 loop tick 8; this invocation ran on Opus as the Fable fallback). Reviewed cold: plan §4 + my cycle-1 section, the rework diff 7c80e50..ddc8833 (one commit, one file: apps/chat/test/watcher-deploy-real.test.js +58/-8; production code byte-identical to what I reviewed in cycle 1), then the running software.

VERDICT: PASS (merge). 0 blocking findings, 0 findings outside the list that change behavior, 2 notes. Nothing committed on the branch; no inline fixes.

FINDINGS FIRST
- F1 (cycle 1, the leaked `app` compose project): CLOSED. The app dir is now `<tmp>/<project>` so compose derives the same name `-p project` tears down. Demonstrated, not argued: unmutated real build 1/1 pass in 105.5 s; afterwards `docker compose ls -a` lists no as87 project and `docker ps -a --filter label=com.docker.compose.service=as87` is empty (the asc-review-as87 receipt project is also gone after its `down -v`).
- AC-11 / M9 (my cycle-1 ask): RED as named. Scratch copy with `const app = join(dir, 'app')` restored (mutation asserted at the one site): fails in 82.4 s at the FIRST AC-11 assertion — `AC-11: no container from this run survives teardown`, actual `['app-as87-1\tproject=app\tworking_dir=/private/tmp/asc-as87-45611-OXL4ke/app']`. Exact red set = 1 (the single opt-in test), exactly the predicted line. The probe is keyed on the run's temp-dir basename (working_dir label / ConfigFiles), not on `project`, which is why it catches the very mismatch that was the bug; the positive control (1 container, 1 project, >=1 image before teardown) passed on the unmutated run, so the empty answer after teardown is not vacuous.
- M10 (mine, past the list): drop `--rmi local` from teardown -> RED in 92.1 s at the THIRD AC-11 assertion only — `AC-11: --rmi local removed the image the build produced`, actual `['asc-as87-45632-eb6cuy-as87:latest']`. So the image half of AC-11 stands on its own falsifier, not on the container half.
- N2 / AS-117 (fail-fast): TAKEN and proven on two refusal shapes I chose, not the implementer's. Scratch copies: (a) `run` returns code 128 for `ls-tree` -> `{"action":"noop","reason":"no-git"}`; (b) `fetchJson` throws -> the AS-84 belt's `{"action":"noop","reason":"error","detail":"probe exploded"}`. Both fail in 0.7 s with the decision and the ops log in the assertion message, versus the 10-minute hang I observed in cycle 1 under M8. AS-117 can close as folded at this merge.
- Two writers at once (M6): M9 and M10 ran concurrently with each other on this host, sharing the `as87` service label and distinct project names; neither run's footprint probe saw the other's container/project, and M10's image assertion filtered on its own `<project>-` prefix. The per-run keying holds under concurrency.
- Host left as found: everything my mutants leaked (container app-as87-1, images app-as87:latest and asc-as87-45632-eb6cuy-as87:latest, network app_default) was removed by hand and re-verified empty; nothing of the reviewer's is left on the docker host.

NOTES (non-blocking, no change requested)
- N1: the fail-fast comment (test line ~108) says "a deploy sets `deploying` synchronously before its first await" — true of performDeploy(), but evaluate() awaits probeRunning() first; the mechanism does not depend on the claim (a 200 ms race window against a >=75 s build), so I left the wording.
- N2: my cycle-1 count prediction (host 536) was wrong and the implementer's 535 is right — AC-11 rides inside the opt-in test, not as a separate test. Recorded so the next reviewer does not chase it.

SWEEP (floor check, after the findings) — cardinality first
- Host `node --test` in the worktree: 535 tests / 534 pass / 1 skipped (opt-in) / 0 fail, exit 0. Master baseline 530 -> +5, unchanged from cycle 1.
- Compose receipt: `/usr/local/bin/docker compose -p asc-review-as87 run --rm --build test` via node spawnSync (docker off PATH) -> `Image asc-review-as87-test Built` (line 59 of the log), 535 tests / 529 pass / 6 skipped (5 git-less container skips + 1 opt-in, line 448 `# opt-in: set AS87_REAL_BUILD=1`) / 0 fail, exit 0; `down -v --remove-orphans` exit 0; project absent from `compose ls -a` afterwards.
- AC-1/2/3/4/5/6/9: production code untouched by the rework (verified by `git diff 7c80e50..ddc8833 --stat`), the cycle-1 reds stand and are not re-run; the tests are present and green in both suites above (heartbeat test, argv pin, composeBuild pass-through, sidebar sentence).
- AC-7: real build unmutated 1/1 pass, 105.5 s (heartbeats >= 5 with `deploying`, log non-empty with AS87-MARKER and `#N` lines). Cycle-1 M7 reds (M1 -> heartbeat red, M6 -> log red) not repeated — the rework did not touch those assertions.
- AC-8: opt-in test registers as 1 skipped in both suites, never a fail.
- AC-10: both counted runs above, receipt line quoted.
- AC-11: positive control + M9 + M10 above. 11 of 11 pass; findings outside the list: 0 blocking.
- Mutants this cycle: 4 named (M9, M10, N2-nogit, N2-error), 4 runs, 4 red, 0 survivors, every red set exactly the predicted assertion.
- Branch hygiene: 4 commits, all `developer-marcus <developer-marcus@agents.american-software.local>`; `git merge-tree --write-tree master feat/AS-87-deploy-heartbeat-and-log` clean; no `.lattice/` paths on the branch; worktree clean (all mutation on scratch copies under scratchpad/agent-qa-priya/as87c2-scratch/, never in the worktree).

Evidence: scratchpad/agent-qa-priya/as87c2-*.log and as87c2-mutate.mjs (mutations applied with a one-site assertion each).
